model: The natural place I'd really like to protect is Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park in central Vietnam. I went there with two friends about three years ago, and it's still one of the best trips I've ever had. The park is famous for its enormous caves, and it's also covered in thick forest, so there's a lot of untouched nature. We did a two-day trek, and the breathtaking scenery made me forget all about work and my phone. At night we camped near a river, and our guide reminded us to leave no trace, so we carried every piece of rubbish back out with us. The reason I want to protect it is that I think it's under threat from mass tourism. Since the area became popular online, more and more hotels and roads have been built, and the guide told us that some of the forest is an important wildlife habitat for rare animals. If they build too many resorts, the animals will lose their homes and the rivers will get polluted. Of course, local people need jobs, so we need to strike a balance. If I had the power, I'd limit the number of visitors each day and make tour companies train their guides properly. I really believe we should keep places like this safe for future generations, because once they're damaged, you can't just fix them.
